cases.note: Nothing here, a link that costs nothing, a digest to check against. The case that has to hold or every refusal below is measuring a function that refuses everything.

Order of cost, and the case that catches getting it wrong. A robot holding the verified bundle must not report itself as waiting for an unmetered link to fetch it — which is what a version that checked metering first would say.
cases.expected: {"decision":"have","detail":"This bundle is already on the disk and has been checked against the manifest. Nothing to fetch.","from":0}

cases.note: §12 binds every gate it applies to the digest, so bytes with no name cannot be bound to. Refused before a bearer is even considered.
cases.expected: {"decision":"refuse","detail":"This release names no bundle digest, so there is nothing to check the bytes against. §12 binds a bench pass to the exact bytes it was taken against, and bytes with no name cannot be bound to — so they are not fetched either.","from":0}

cases.note: §34.1: offline is the ordinary state, not a fault. Nothing is lost — the manifest is already here and the transfer resumes when a link returns.
cases.expected: {"decision":"no_bearer","detail":"No bearer is up, so there is nothing to fetch over. That is the ordinary state for most of a robot's life (§34.1) and nothing about the update is lost by it — the release manifest is already here and the transfer resumes when a link returns.","from":0}

cases.note: §34.3. Hundreds of megabytes per robot over cellular is a bill a fleet discovers at the end of the month, so a bulk class waits and the wait is visible.
cases.expected: {"decision":"wait_for_unmetered","detail":"An OS image is the largest bulk transfer this system has, and `wwan0` is assumed metered. It waits for an unmetered link (§34.3). Nothing is lost by waiting, and a fleet that downloaded hundreds of megabytes per robot over cellular would find out at the end of the month.","from":0}

cases.note: The same refusal, and the sentence says `assumed` rather than `declared`. A vendor who thinks their Wi-Fi is free needs to know the robot does not, and that it is one line of configuration away.
cases.expected: {"decision":"wait_for_unmetered","detail":"An OS image is the largest bulk transfer this system has, and `wlan0` is assumed metered. It waits for an unmetered link (§34.3). Nothing is lost by waiting, and a fleet that downloaded hundreds of megabytes per robot over cellular would find out at the end of the month.","from":0}

cases.note: The partial is keyed to the digest, so it cannot be another image’s tail. The offset is on the plan rather than left for a caller to work out.
cases.expected: {"decision":"resume","detail":"Resuming at 40000 bytes of 100000. The partial is keyed to this bundle's digest, so it cannot be a different image's tail.","from":40000}

cases.note: Not a partial of this bundle at all. Resuming would append this image’s tail to something else’s and the mismatch would surface after the whole transfer, which on a poor link is hours.
cases.expected: {"decision":"discard_and_fetch","detail":"There are 140000 bytes here for a bundle the manifest says is 100000. A partial cannot be larger than what it is part of, so this is left over from something else. It is discarded and the transfer starts again.","from":0}

cases.note: The test is `partial >= size`, and this is the equals. A partial that is exactly the whole length is not a partial: either the transfer finished and nothing recorded it, or these are somebody else's bytes of the same length. Both are answered by discarding and starting again, and an edition testing `>` alone resumes from the end of a file and sends nothing.
cases.expected: {"decision":"discard_and_fetch","detail":"There are 100000 bytes here for a bundle the manifest says is 100000. A partial cannot be larger than what it is part of, so this is left over from something else. It is discarded and the transfer starts again.","from":0}

cases.note: Every manifest a Hub serves today. The "cannot be larger than what it is part of" branch is unreachable without a declared size, so a resume is the only honest answer and the sentence says how far it got without claiming a total.
cases.expected: {"decision":"resume","detail":"Resuming at 40000 bytes. The partial is keyed to this bundle's digest, so it cannot be a different image's tail.","from":40000}

cases.note: Blank to `trim()`, so bytes with no name, refused before a bearer is considered. An edition that kept the byte-order mark would fetch an image no gate can be bound to.
cases.expected: {"decision":"refuse","detail":"This release names no bundle digest, so there is nothing to check the bytes against. §12 binds a bench pass to the exact bytes it was taken against, and bytes with no name cannot be bound to — so they are not fetched either.","from":0}

cases.note: Not blank to `trim()`, so the fetch is planned. Every edition must plan it; whether the Hub should ever have served such a digest is the Hub’s question.
